class.name: StairsBody
class.brief_description: Kinematic character body that walks up and down stairs inside its own move.
class.description: Kinematic character body with stair stepping built into its own move, rather than wrapped around [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide]. A frame pays for one set of sweeps instead of the slide's plus the step check's. Replaces [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide] entirely, so none of [CharacterBody3D]'s API exists here. The getters keep its names where no native method is in the way. Set [member velocity], optionally [member desired_velocity], then call [method move_and_stair_step] from [method Node._physics_process]. The floor, wall and ceiling getters, the platform velocity and the contact list describe where the last [method move_and_stair_step] left the body, and only a move updates them. After moving the body any other way (setting its transform, reparenting it, carrying it without moves), call [method move_and_stair_step] before reading them. A body at rest skips its checks: with no [member velocity] and no [member desired_velocity], on a static floor that carries it nowhere, it makes one shape query per move in their place while neither it nor its floor has moved and nothing that could move into it touches it, and the getters keep the last move's answers. Static bodies, [StairsBody] nodes that collide with it and crowd neighbours are passed over, since none of them can move into it. A change to its own collider, such as a crouch resizing, moving or switching off a shape, wakes it, and a body that starts inside something only rests once it is out. [member velocity] has to be exactly zero. Physics queries per frame, the budget this class is built around: [codeblock lang=text] walking on flat ground 2 (the move sweep, the contact test; within 1 cm of the last one on a static floor, a shape query instead) standing still 1 (a shape query, once at rest on a static floor) pressed into a wall 2 (the same two; the step attempt is cached) intent off the motion +1 (a sweep along intent, which only looks for a step; only standing still or against a face intent pushes into) climbing a step 5 (move sweep, up, forward, down, contact test) leaving a floor +1 (the floor probe, only where contact is lost) on a moving platform +1 (the carry, as its own sweep) on a walk grid 0 (see walk_grid; the sweeps take over where it cannot answer) [/codeblock] Assumes world up is [constant Vector3.UP].

method.name: get_contact_collider
method.description: The object the contact at [param index] belongs to, or [code]null[/code] if it has been freed since the move. See [method get_contact_count] for which contacts are listed.

method.name: get_contact_collider_id
method.description: Instance id of the object the contact at [param index] belongs to. Cheaper than [method get_contact_collider] when only comparing ids.

method.name: get_contact_count
method.description: Number of contacts the last [method move_and_stair_step] made. Listed: each slide sweep's contact, the sweeps of a step the body committed, a moving floor's carry, the floor probe when it set the body down, and the resting contacts after the move, floor included. Not listed: the sweeps of a step that was refused, and resting contacts with bodies on [member step_ignore_layers] unless the body is standing on one. Cleared at the start of every move. A collider may appear more than once; the order carries no meaning.

method.name: get_contact_normal
method.description: Normal of the contact at [param index], pointing from the collider toward the body.

method.name: get_contact_position
method.description: Global position of the contact at [param index].

method.name: get_floor_normal
method.description: Normal of the floor found by the last move. Only meaningful while [method is_on_floor] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: get_platform_velocity
method.description: Velocity of the floor the body stands on, added to [member velocity] when the body leaves it.

method.name: get_wall_normal
method.description: Normal of the wall hit by the last move. Only meaningful while [method is_on_wall] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: is_on_ceiling
method.description: Whether the last move hit a ceiling.

method.name: is_on_floor
method.description: Whether the body ended the last move on a floor. Not updated when the body is moved any other way; see the class description.

method.name: is_on_walk_grid
method.description: Whether the last [method move_and_stair_step] was made on [member walk_grid] rather than by sweeps.

method.name: is_on_wall
method.description: Whether the last move hit a wall, or the body is being held still against one.

method.name: is_step_surface
method.description: Whether a step may be committed onto [param body]: anything the physics server is not simulating (static geometry, kinematic platforms, frozen rigid bodies) and not on [param ignore_layers]. A step is a teleport rather than a solve, so setting the body down on a simulating one leaves the solver to separate them by moving the only thing that can move, which raises the surface and offers the next frame a fresh step. Measured under Jolt: a loose 0.45 x 0.3 x 0.45 m crate lifted the body 1.085 m and left at 5.6 m/s, the same at 10 kg and 30 kg.

method.name: move_and_stair_step
method.description: Moves the body by [member velocity] for one physics frame, stepping up and down stairs. Call it from [method Node._physics_process]. [param time_scale] stretches the frame for a body moved less often than every frame: a body moved every other frame passes [code]2.0[/code] on the frames it moves and skips the call on the others, with [member velocity] and [member desired_velocity] left at their real values. Crowd separation reaches as far as such a body walks, and a push it is given on a frame it skips is kept for its next move.

members.member: Layers of other [StairsBody] nodes this one keeps apart from by crowd separation rather than by collision; leave those layers out of [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask]. Once per physics frame, before the first member moves, members overlapping by more than 5 mm are pushed back to touching, each taking half, and shallower overlap is left alone so a still crowd can rest; a member takes its push as part of its own next move, so the push is swept against the world with it. Each move's own motion is also kept out of the neighbours; a member wedged between neighbours has its own motion cut until it fits, down to none, and counts the neighbours it was wedged against as touched. Neighbours are read from a snapshot each member updates as it moves, so a member moved or turned by other code during the frame, after its own move, is seen as its move left it until the next frame. Footprints are capsules lying flat, measured once from the shapes' bounds, so members never stand on each other. Neighbours touched are listed as contacts, with a horizontal normal pointing back at this body.
Horizontal intent for this frame. Drives the step probe when velocity has been pinned near zero by the face it is pushing into. Cleared after each move.
Steepest surface that counts as floor, in radians.
Allow a step this frame even when airborne. Cleared after each move.

Slide iterations for the main move. On the floor, a slide stops against a wall met within 15 degrees of head-on rather than sliding along it, as [CharacterBody3D] does under its default [member CharacterBody3D.wall_min_slide_angle]. In a crowd pressed together, each further slide meets the next neighbour.
Smallest distance a step probe looks ahead, whatever the tick rate.
Collision margin used by every sweep.
How far the floor probe reaches down to stay on the ground or step down. Negative follows [member step_height].
Max height the body can step up onto.

Collision layers a step is never committed onto, though the body still collides with them: bodies too small or too self-driving to be a stair. Taken out of the body's mask while the step and floor-probe sweeps run, so those sweeps see the surface underneath instead. A floor on these layers holds the body up but never carries it as a platform: [method get_platform_velocity] stays zero on it.
Slide iterations for the forward leg of a step.
Velocity in m/s. Written back after each move: clipped against what the body hit, and with any downward part zeroed while on the floor.

A [StairsWalkGrid] to walk on instead of sweeping, or [code]null[/code]. A move is made on the grid, with no physics query, when the body is on a floor the grid baked, is not rising, stands within 5 mm of the grid's floor, and no static shape the grid left out and no body that may move, on a layer in [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask], is within its reach. On the grid, the body slides along boxes that stand higher than [member step_height], steps up onto the highest top under its footprint that is no higher than that, and steps down within the step-down reach. Otherwise the move is made by sweeps, as it is when the grid cannot finish it (a drop past the step-down reach, a ceiling met stepping up, the body already inside a box), and the next moves return to the grid once the body stands on a baked box again. Other StairsBody nodes are not among the bodies that may move the grid tracks (see [StairsWalkGrid]): bodies on the grid keep apart only by crowd separation, so set [member crowd_layers] on a crowd that walks on it. Set this to [code]null[/code] and back at any time. Crowd separation, the signals and the getters work as they do with sweeps; see [method is_on_walk_grid].

signal.name: stepped
signal.description: Emitted on any stair step, in either direction, after the direction-specific one. [param delta] is the height the body moved, in metres: positive up, negative down.

signal.name: stepped_down
signal.description: Emitted when the floor probe has set the body down onto a lower surface. [param drop] is how far it went down, in metres, and is positive. It is never more than the whole move's descent, so a move that ends higher than it started emits none.

signal.name: stepped_up
signal.description: Emitted when the body has been raised onto a higher surface. [param rise] is how far it went up, in metres, and is positive.
